detail:
Cleveland Clinic's overview describes management that begins with the cause: treating underlying conditions and reviewing medicines that lower blood pressure, since adjusting a contributing drug is a clinician decision that can change symptoms. Everyday measures include changing positions slowly, staying hydrated, eating smaller meals, sleeping with the head of the bed raised, and using compression stockings or an abdominal binder to reduce blood pooling.

For neurogenic orthostatic hypotension that persists despite these steps, clinicians may prescribe medicines that raise standing blood pressure, such as midodrine, droxidopa, or fludrocortisone, and they monitor for high blood pressure when lying down, a known trade-off of this treatment group.

Talk to your doctor before starting or changing any medication.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material.
summary: Cleveland Clinic describes treatment that starts with finding and treating the cause and reviewing medicines, then simple measures like rising slowly, fluids, and compression, with prescription medicines for some people.
takeaways: rise slowly and sit back down if symptoms start
fluid and salt changes help some people; ask your doctor for targets
compression stockings or abdominal binders can reduce pooling
midodrine and similar medicines are prescription decisions for your doctor
title: Managing orthostatic hypotension
